_comment: The mcp capability manifest for the published artifact, and the page's own allowlist.
One source for two things that must never disagree: the `capabilities.mcp` value passed
to the Artifact tool at publish time, and the tools the page will forward a call to.
`server` is the DISPLAY NAME of the connector in the publishing account's claude.ai
Settings -> Connectors. It is not a URL and carries no token: calls run with the
`tools` MUST be the exact upstream tool names that connector exposes. There is no
wildcard, and a wrong name fails at runtime with not_in_manifest.
`enabled: false` drops a server from the published manifest entirely. The page then
shows that system as not configured and the skill stages its steps with a named owner,
rather than the run failing halfway. Turn one on only once its `tools` list is real.
`verified` records whether the tool names were confirmed against a live listTools()
call, or only transcribed from references/connector-map.md.

servers.purpose: Every system. Slack stays here rather than on the native Claude Slack connector, which has no tool to add or remove a channel member — see references/connector-map.md.
_tools_note: Zapier MCP is GENERIC: it does NOT expose one tool per app action. There is no
google_workspace_admin_..._raw_request tool to name here. The flow is:
All six names were read off the live connector on 2026-09-12. Note the infix: the
execute and discover tools are *_zapier_*, NOT the bare discover_actions /
execute_read_action / execute_write_action the UI display names suggest.
